style.vernacular: Victorian seaside capital: long curving promenade terraces of former boarding houses in cream and white painted render and stucco with bays, pitched slate roofs and chimney stacks; Georgian merchants houses in the old town; grey and pink Manx stone and slate churches, farms and cottages (some whitewashed, a few thatched) in the countryside, small red-brick Victorian civic and market buildings, and modern office, hospital and college blocks around the edges.
style.ornament: Victorian bay windows and balconies on promenade terraces, white-painted sash windows, Matcham theatre plasterwork, battlemented Gothic-revival country houses, Celtic crosses and the Three Legs of Man emblem, slate-hung gables, rubble stone field walls and thatch on a few fishermens cottages.

sources.what: Loch Promenade 1870s boarding-house terrace, Castle Mona 1804, Georgian merchants houses (Isola on John Street), Gaiety Theatre 1900, Tower of Refuge 1832
